sections.preamble: You answer questions about a single medical image. Follow the answer format requested in the user message exactly.

content.text:
This is one axial slice of a T2-weighted fat-suppressed MRI (radiological convention: patient right on image left, anterior at top). It contains a fibrous soft-tissue tumor.

The left panel is the clean image; the right panel shows numbered marks. Choose the ONE mark that lies inside the tumor, as close to its centre as possible. End your reply with a final line exactly: ANSWER: <mark number>

content.thinking:
I'm looking at this knee axial slice, trying to identify the structures—the dark region appears to be the distal femur with fat-suppressed marrow, while a heterogeneous hyperintense area anteriorly near the prepatellar region could represent the tumor.

I'm checking which label number best matches the position of the large mass by comparing its center coordinates to candidate marker positions, and landing on 115 as the closest match.

content.text:
I read the large, homogeneous, dark mass in the centre of the slice as the fibrous tumour, since fibrous tumours are typically dark on T2. This is an uncertain call. That mass could instead be bone marrow suppressed by the fat-saturation, and I did not find a clearer candidate. The heterogeneous bright tissue at the front looks like subcutaneous or prepatellar tissue, so I excluded it.

The mass spans roughly x 290–650 and y 215–610 on the clean panel, which puts its centre near (470, 410). Mark 115 sits at about (525, 395) on that panel, about 55 px from the centre. Mark 95 is about 96 px away, and the other marks are farther or fall outside the mass. Mark 115 is therefore the closest to the centre.

ANSWER: 115
